readiness: Receive explicit permission for this physical run and confirm both devices are available; preparation is not permission to operate them.
Confirm live Watch/phone identifiers, installed matched build/source and OS, wrist/Crown orientation, current class schedule and running/intentional-Stop state.
Use one input owner. Rehearse phone and Watch screen capture and one reversible touch action in their current screen-sharing views; stop if a view or target is ambiguous.
Rehearse a small physical Crown turn or obtain an operator for it. Simulator Crown transport is not a physical input driver; do not mark automated Crown delivery established without device evidence.

Open an already available music app on the phone, select the planned track, verify the intended output, start quietly, and independently confirm playback advancement. No purchase, sign-in or new destination is assumed.
Prepare the before/failure/after journal destinations and the established Watch/phone sysdiagnose path. Copy small journals before long downloads; a capture request is not a completed archive.
Record pre-run class/settings/runtime intent and prepare restoration. Defer any arm requiring a reset, uninstalled comparison build or unavailable route rather than changing real teaching context.
commonControls: Keep the installed build, music app, track, output, quiet nonzero baseline, Watch orientation, runtime intent and transition history fixed except for the arm's named factor.
Record process/native-control identity where logs expose it; a retained-state arm is inconclusive if process/control retention is unknown or changed unexpectedly.
Save pre-input timer ring and phone state before any Watch refresh, page switch or Crown movement. A visible ring is not proof of an internal baseline or command destination.
stopConditions: Stop input immediately on an unexpected zero, silent output, no response, lost connection, passcode lock, ambiguous source/UI or unexpected output.

Preserve pre-recovery screenshots/recording and mark incident; attempt failure journals within 30 seconds, then prioritize one prompt Watch and phone sysdiagnose request over retries or large transfers.
Only after preservation, perform one marked recovery: same-source embedded media page/return or phone volume control. Record which action works; do not treat recovery as proof of cause.
Pause test music at the planned end; mark audio_stopped and run_stopped, restore class/runtime intent without clearing class context, then copy after journals.
evidenceLimits: Operator marks and file references are not independently validated device evidence. No finite set of clean runs proves an intermittent issue fixed.

The public app exposes no native volume scalar/readiness callback. First outgoing scalars and endpoint/session identifiers require retained system records; missing/redacted records are missing evidence, not zero or no command.
Phone volume indicators are not exact acoustic measurements. Known Crown direction requires a physical recording/operator statement; Simulator private event subtypes do not decode it.
Home/standalone Now Playing can change runtime and native state. Capture the failure first, and record automatic recovery or process replacement as a deviation.

scenarios.changedFactor: Elapsed idle interval only; no provider, route or phone volume change
supports: The same retained control fails its first return adjustment after a known working reference.
weakens: Matched repeated retained runs remain responsive with expected first values.

Known small Crown intent/direction and first native outgoing scalar if retained

steps: Open TeachingTimer, confirm/reuse the planned class/runtime intent, and establish quiet working phone playback and timer Crown response.
Save a reference ring/phone level. Leave the timer selected and permit wrist-down for 10–15 minutes without input or polling gestures.
Wake, save the pre-input ring/phone level, make one known small up turn, and record the first request/result before changing pages.
If normal, make one small opposite turn while staying nonzero; otherwise follow the common stop/capture procedure.

Allow wrist-down. Use only phone controls to set another quiet nonzero level B; record before/after phone state and exact mark times.
Wake the timer without refresh or page changes; capture the ring and current phone level before the first small known up turn.
Record the first outgoing request and audible result. Test Home/return only in a separate repeat, noting any runtime recovery or control replacement.

steps: Establish a working Apple Music/phone-speaker reference; save state and retain the Watch control without force-quitting.
Pause Apple Music on the phone, open an already available Amazon Music or YouTube Music source, and play quietly on the same output; verify the first player is paused.
Confirm source/output independently on the phone. Return directly to timer without refresh/media; capture before one known small up turn.
Preserve any failure before visiting TeachingTimer media or standalone Now Playing. Record a provider change as such, not proof of a new OS audio session.

Retain the timer control, pause and resume the same track on the phone, and record both actions.

Seek system session identifiers during later analysis; call this pause/resume unless a new OS audio session is actually established.

limits: Startup order is a trigger condition, not an identified mechanism. Different control lifetime or runtime history makes the pairing confounded; label it instead of assuming equivalence.

weakens: Both timings behave equivalently under matched state, or failure occurs long after synchronization.

steps: Establish a working quiet baseline; dim/wake with the same selected timer, source/output and runtime intent.
Capture pre-input state and make one small known up turn at the first usable wake; record the actual timing rather than claiming precise synchronization.
Restore the baseline and prepare a separate new notebook with the same wake sequence; wait about 3 seconds before the matched turn.
Compare actual timing and first requests. This is a diagnostic comparison, not a production startup delay.

weakens: A verified downward gesture legitimately reaches minimum, zero precedes input, or both signed references behave normally.

scenarios.title: Embedded progress extrapolation versus source updates
scenarios.hypothesis: TeachingTimer's embedded native media presentation may fail to advance between valid source position updates.
scenarios.changedFactor: Embedded versus standalone native view; deliberate phone seek only as a later separate step
supports: Embedded position catches up after reentry/seek then freezes while independent playback and standalone progress advance.
weakens: Both native views stale together, or the actual source stops advancing; source/transport remains a candidate.
requiredEvidence: Two timed embedded ring frames with independent actual phone song positions and play state
Exact page/wake/dim/seek times and embedded view-generation journal
Separate standalone Now Playing comparison with same phone source
Recovery command continuity and runtime/class state before/after
steps: Use an already playable short finite track such as Brian Eno An Ending (Ascent), catalog714861225; keep source/output fixed and verify phone progress.
Open TeachingTimer's embedded media page and capture two positions at least 20 seconds apart while the display remains awake; record phone positions independently.
If stale, capture it before leaving. Only then open Apple's standalone Now Playing app for the same-source comparison; record any runtime/foreground change.

Return to TeachingTimer and, as a separately marked step, seek once on the phone to test discrete position updates versus ongoing extrapolation. Do not conflate black content, wrong source, stalled progress or failed transport controls.
